question: The parents of a 4-year-old present to the pediatrician because they are concerned about the poor growth and odd behavior of their son. Their son has been at the 10th percentile for growth since birth and they have noticed that his skin seems to have a bluish hue to it whenever he cries or is agitated. Recently, they have noticed that when he squats it seems to relieve these symptoms. What was the embryologic cause of this patient's current symptoms?

options.opa: Failure of the aorticopulmonary septum to spiral
options.opb: Failure of the ductus arteriosus to obliterate
options.opd: Failure of septum primum and septum secundum to fuse

analysis: The symptoms described in the case are consistent with Tetralogy of Fallot, a congenital heart defect. The bluish hue of the skin (cyanosis) upon crying or agitation is due to decreased pulmonary blood flow resulting in deoxygenated blood being circulated. The relief of symptoms upon squatting is known as the squatting position, which increases systemic vascular resistance and decreases the right-to-left shunting of blood, improving oxygenation. This condition is caused by the anterosuperior displacement of the aorticopulmonary septum during embryologic development.
